literal: Wealth lost even-when, old-ties cherishing kinsmen with-indeed are-found.
translation: Even when one's wealth is lost, the cherishing of old ties is found only among kinsmen.
modern: ஒருவருடைய செல்வம் அழிந்த காலத்திலும், பழைய உறவைப் பாராட்டி அன்பு செலுத்தும் பண்பு சுற்றத்தாரிடமே உள்ளது.
explanation: This couplet highlights the enduring nature of true kinship. The word 'paṟṟu' generally means attachment or hold, but in this context, it specifically refers to wealth or resources that one holds onto. Even when a person loses all their wealth and becomes destitute, it is only their true relatives who will remember their old ties ('paḻaimai') and continue to cherish them. The emphatic suffix 'ē' in 'kaṇṇē' stresses that this unconditional loyalty is an exclusive trait found only among one's kin.
